title: Limits of Trigonometric Functions
notes: **Fundamental limit.** lim(x→0) sin x/x = 1 and lim(x→0) tan x/x = 1; these follow from the squeeze theorem applied to the unit-circle sector areas.
**Cosine form.** lim(x→0) (1 − cos x)/x² = 1/2, obtained by writing 1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2) and applying the sine limit twice.
**Worked example.** lim(x→0) sin 5x / sin 3x = (5/3) · [lim sin 5x/(5x)] / [lim sin 3x/(3x)] = 5/3.
**Radian requirement.** These limits hold only when x is in radians; using degrees introduces a factor of π/180 and changes every result.
**General angles.** For lim(x→a) sin(x − a)/(x − a), substitute u = x − a so the limit reduces to lim(u→0) sin u/u = 1.
**Exam caution.** Convert expressions like 1 − cos²x to sin²x before taking the limit, and check that the argument of every sine tends to zero.
summary: Trigonometric limits rest on lim(x→0) sin x/x = 1 and lim(x→0) (1 − cos x)/x² = 1/2, with angles always measured in radians.
